questions.question:
2.5
Sphere Y, carrying a charge of −5 × 10⁻⁷ C, is now fixed at point P and sphere Z, carrying a charge of −4 × 10⁻⁷ C, is fixed 0.04 m to the right of sphere X.

The NET FORCE acting on sphere X is 0.0427 N at point A.

Is the surface frictionless? Choose from YES or NO. Explain the answer by means of a calculation.

(6)
questions.answer:
2.5

NOTE: Ignore if negative charges are substituted.

OPTION 1

FXY = kQXQY/r²
FXY = (9 × 10⁹)(3 × 10⁻⁷)(5 × 10⁻⁷)/(0.05)²
FXY = 0.54 N

FXZ = kQXQZ/r²
FXZ = (9 × 10⁹)(3 × 10⁻⁷)(4 × 10⁻⁷)/(0.04)²
FXZ = 0.68 N

Fnet(E) = FXZ + FXY
= 0.68 − 0.54
= 0.14 N

No
Fnet(E) > Fnet

OPTION 2

Enet = kQ/r² + kQ/r²
Enet = (9 × 10⁹)(5 × 10⁻⁷)/(0.05)² − (9 × 10⁹)(4 × 10⁻⁷)/(0.04)²
Enet = 450 000 N·C⁻¹

Fnet = qE
Fnet = (3 × 10⁻⁷)(450 000)
Fnet = 0.14 N

No
Fnet(E) > Fnet

OPTION 3

Fnet(E) = kQXQY/r² − kQXQZ/r²
Fnet(E) = (9 × 10⁹)(3 × 10⁻⁷)(5 × 10⁻⁷)/(0.05)² − (9 × 10⁹)(3 × 10⁻⁷)(4 × 10⁻⁷)/(0.04)²
Fnet(E) = 0.14 N

0.0427 = 0.14 − f
f = 0.0923 N

No

Two point charges, Q1 = +5 × 10⁻⁶ C and Q2 = −3 × 10⁻⁶ C, are separated by a distance of 0.2 m in a vacuum.

Calculate the magnitude of the electrostatic force between the charges.

(3)

3.2
Two point charges, Q1 = +2 × 10⁻⁸ C and Q2 = +8 × 10⁻⁸ C, are separated by a distance of 0.3 m.

3.2.1 Calculate the magnitude of the electric field at a point P, which is 0.1 m from Q1 and 0.2 m from Q2, on the line joining the charges.

3.2.2 Draw the electric field lines for the two charges.

(7)
questions.answer:
3.2.1

E1 = kQ1/r1²
E1 = (9 × 10⁹)(2 × 10⁻⁸)/(0.1)²
E1 = 1.8 × 10⁴ N·C⁻¹ (away from Q1)

E2 = kQ2/r2²
E2 = (9 × 10⁹)(8 × 10⁻⁸)/(0.2)²
E2 = 1.8 × 10⁴ N·C⁻¹ (away from Q2)

Since both fields are in opposite directions:
Enet = E2 − E1
Enet = 1.8 × 10⁴ − 1.8 × 10⁴
Enet = 0 N·C⁻¹

(4)

3.2.2

Criteria:
• Field lines originate from positive charges and terminate on negative charges (or extend to infinity for positive charges).
• Field lines do not cross.
• Correct direction indicated.
• Correct shape (repulsion pattern for like charges).

(3)

(7)

(7)
questions.answer:
3.3.1

Accepted labels:

w — Fg / weight / mg
FE — Electric force / electrostatic force

Notes:
• Mark awarded for label and arrow.
• Any other additional force(s): Max 3/4
• If everything correct, but no arrows: Max 3/4

(4)

3.3.2

FE = qE
FE = (4 × 10⁻⁸)(2 × 10⁴)

w = mg
w = (0.5 × 10⁻³)(9.8)
w = 4.9 × 10⁻³ N

tan θ = FE/w
tan θ = (8 × 10⁻⁴)/(4.9 × 10⁻³)

θ = 9.27°

5.3
Two point charges, Q1 = +4 × 10⁻⁶ C and Q2 = +9 × 10⁻⁶ C, are separated by a distance of 0.5 m.

5.3.1 Calculate the distance from Q1 at which the net electric field is zero.

5.3.2 Sketch the electric field pattern for the two charges.

(6)
questions.answer:
5.3.1

Let the distance from Q1 be x. Then the distance from Q2 is (0.5 − x).

E1 = E2
kQ1/x² = kQ2/(0.5 − x)²
Q1/x² = Q2/(0.5 − x)²
(4 × 10⁻⁶)/x² = (9 × 10⁻⁶)/(0.5 − x)²
4/x² = 9/(0.5 − x)²
2/x = 3/(0.5 − x)
2(0.5 − x) = 3x
1 − 2x = 3x
1 = 5x
x = 0.2 m

(3)

5.3.2

• Field lines do not cross.
• Correct shape (repulsion pattern).
